questions.stem: In triangle ABC, b = 7 cm, c = 9 cm, and angle A = 52 degrees. Find side a to 1 decimal place.
A triangle has sides a = 8 cm, b = 6 cm, and c = 10 cm. Find angle A to 1 decimal place.
In triangle PQR, q = 5 cm, r = 8 cm, and angle P = 120 degrees. Find side p to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: p^2 = 25 + 64 - 2(5)(8)cos(120) = 89 - 80(-0.5) = 89 + 40 = 129. p = sqrt(129) = 11.4 cm (1 d.p.). Note: cos(120) is negative, so the subtraction becomes addition.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 7 cm, and 10 cm. Find the largest angle to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: The largest angle is opposite the longest side (10 cm). cos(C) = (25 + 49 - 100)/70 = -26/70 = -0.3714. C = cos^(-1)(-0.3714) = 111.8 degrees (1 d.p.). The negative cosine indicates an obtuse angle.

questions.stem: Two ships leave a port. Ship A sails 12 km and Ship B sails 18 km. The angle between their paths is 65 degrees. How far apart are the ships? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
